US Proposes Adding Copper, Potash, 4 Others to Critical Minerals List
Potash, silicon, copper, silver, rhenium, and lead are added in a three-year update to be formally posted on Aug. 26 for public comment.

The Interior Department is proposing to add six mineral commodities to the list of critical minerals as part of the Trump administration’s effort to incentivize domestic production and processing of metals, minerals, and rare earth elements vital to the nation’s economy and national defense.
Potash, silicon, copper, silver, rhenium, and lead are recommended by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) for inclusion on the list, which will be formally posted in the
Federal Register
on Aug. 26.
